FIP.thesis_summary: A signed $1.52 billion sale of the Long Ridge power plant to MARA, awaiting only a change-of-control approval from the energy regulator, guided to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026 and cutting total debt from $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion; the shares at $4.23 sit near their fifty-two-week low against a $9.00 event-resolved value and a realistic $2.75 deal-break price.
FIP.dated_milestone: Change-of-control approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, application filed 8 May 2026 in docket EC26-92, guided by management to arrive in the middle of the third quarter of 2026, with the sale closing by 30 September 2026 on the seller's guidance. Nearest scheduled checkpoint: second-quarter 2026 results after the close on Wednesday 5 August 2026, with the conference call at 8:00 a.m. Eastern on Thursday 6 August 2026.
FIP.kill_risk: [CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTIONS] The '14x private-market mark' that anchors the entire sum-of-the-parts is not what the buyer says it paid. MARA's own 30 April 2026 announcement states Long Ridge contributes approximately $144 million of annualised adjusted EBITDA (second-half 2025 basis, reflecting the February 2025 hedge swaps and the June 2025 capacity payments) - i.e. the buyer underwrote roughly 10.5x, not 14x. FIP.dossier_note: Buy it now, and size it as a levered stub with a live event rather than as an arbitrage with a floor. The event is genuine. A definitive agreement was signed on 29 April 2026 to sell the Long Ridge power plant to MARA for about $1.52 billion, the regulatory application was filed on 8 May in docket EC26-92, the buyer cleared its bondholder consents in June, no financing contingency exists, and management has guided to approval by the middle of the third quarter. Nothing about it has fired, and the shares have actually fallen since the announcement, so none of the re-rating has been spent. At $4.23, close to the fifty-two-week low of $3.90 and against a high of $7.94, you are being paid to wait for a transaction that reduces total debt from $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion and saves about $30 million of interest a year, on a company whose surviving railroads grew earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation 31% year over year. There is no wash-out worth waiting for; this is the wash-out. Two things keep this from being the maximum-conviction version of this setup. The first is the floor. The entry carried into this review assumes $3.90 of downside protection, and that number is a chart level, not a recovery value. Book equity is negative $303.1 million, there is no net cash, operating cash flow was negative $69.4 million last quarter, and the filing's own liquidity assurance is expressly conditioned on this sale closing. A deal-break realistically prices the shares

VRDN.thesis_summary: The catalyst has already fired: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) for thyroid eye disease on 26 June 2026, four days ahead of its 30 June target date and with a broader label than expected - and the stock is at $19.70 a month later, so the re-rating we were waiting to be paid for has been spent without paying, leaving roughly 52% upside to a $30 good-launch value against 57% downside to an $8.50 cash-based floor.
VRDN.dated_milestone: FDA approval granted 26 June 2026 (the target decision date was 30 June 2026) - fired, favourably and early, with the launch beginning the same week. Remaining calendar, none of it hard or binding: second-quarter results expected around 5 August 2026 (a stub month of launch revenue); management's guidance of broad insurance coverage within six to nine months of launch, pointing to roughly December 2026 through March 2027; a company-controlled approval filing for elegrobart targeted for the first quarter of 2027; and a European decision expected during 2027 on the application accepted in February 2026.
VRDN.kill_risk: [REFUTED] The catalyst has fired and nothing dated, binding or agency-controlled replaces it. Verified against the company's own 26 June 2026 release: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) 'for the treatment of thyroid eye disease regardless of thyroid eye disease activity or duration', four days ahead of the 30 June 2026 PDUFA target action date, with no advisory committee, no complete response letter, and immediate launch -- physicians 'can prescribe Lumvoa tomorrow'. That is the best available version of the event this sleeve underwrote, and the tape refused it: the live quote is $19.70

VRDN.dossier_note:
This is a pass for now, and the reason is simple enough to state in one sentence: we were underwriting a dated regulatory decision, that decision arrived on 26 June 2026 - early, clean, and with a broader label than we expected - and the stock is at $19.70 a month later. When the best available outcome of a binary event does not pay, the market is pricing something the event did not address, and continuing to hold is no longer the trade we sized. It is a different trade wearing the old trade's clothes.

What the market is pricing is the 30 March 2026 data on elegrobart, the under-the-skin follow-on. That trial met its goal but at roughly 36 to 45 placebo-adjusted percentage points against about 64 for the approved infused drug, and the shares fell roughly a third that day and never recovered. The self-administered format is what was supposed to carry a chronic-disease franchise over a decade. A weaker version of it is a smaller company, and an approval for the infused drug does not repair that.

Two corrections to our own file, pulling in opposite directions. First, the balance sheet is much stronger than we carried: the company raised $350 million gross in May 2026 - shares at $17.00 plus 1.75% notes due 2032 - and collected a $75 million approval milestone from its royalty partner in late June, so cash is roughly $1.0 billion, not $600 million. The dilution risk we flagged as the way the floor breaks has already been taken, before the event, which is good treasury disciplin

EYPT.thesis_summary: The underwritten catalyst is spent. EyePoint's LUGANO pivotal Phase 3 — the readout the board dated to 2026-07-31 — fired on 2026-08-17 and MISSED its prespecified primary endpoint (change from baseline in BCVA vs on-label 2mg aflibercept) in the full randomized dataset. Non-inferiority appears only in an analysis the company itself labels ad hoc, excluding 9 of 211 DURAVYU patients (4%) who lost 15+ letters, against ZERO comparable cases in the control arm; the attached p=0.0096 is nominal and carries no regulatory weight. The tape resolved on the loss leg: $14.75 (2026-08-14) to $4.87 (2026-08-25 close, FMP), about -67%, with the 52-week low of $3.95 set the same week — i.e. BELOW the board's claimed $5.50 "floor," which was an assertion rather than an asset. The board's $37.50 target was RBC's pre-readout number; RBC withdrew it on 2026-08-18, cutting to $5 and downgrading to Sector Perform (Chardan $65 to $5, Jefferies $30 to $8, Jones $43 to $20, Citi to $17, JPMorgan to Neutral). A successor exists but is NOT the event we owned: LUCIA, the second identically designed pivotal, is fully enrolled with topline guided by the company to "the fourth quarter of 2026" (press reporting narrows it to October, not a company-fixed date), with an NDA in 1H 2027 contingent on it. That is a fresh, undated, unhedged binary in front of a near-certain financing — not the resolution of the dated event this seat was underwritten on.
EYPT.kill_risk: My load-bearing claim is that the edge is spent because LUGANO fired and failed and the successor is undated. Two credible refutations survive. (1) TIMING: the company's WRITTEN guidance is "Q4 2026," but sell-side and trade press since 2026-08-17 report LUCIA topline "expected in October." If EyePoint firms that into a fixed date, a re-underwritable dated binary sets up roughly six weeks after a FIRED exit — the classic sell-the-wreck-then-watch-it-double failure mode, and from a $4.87 base with ~$180m of cash behind it the win leg is a multiple, not a spread. My status is correct on today's record but has a short shelf life; re-poll before the sleeve treats this name as permanently dead. (2) VALUATION DIRECTION: at $408m cap against $180.5m cash and no borrowed debt, roughly $228m of program value is still priced in — this is NOT a max-fear print, so the risk to my $1.75 lose-leg is that it is far below where the tape would actually clear, while my 0.30 win_prob may itself be generous given XBI near a five-year high makes market-implied probabilities structurally rich. Residual risk cuts both ways: the floor is too low for a tactical mark and the entry is not cheap enough for a fresh binary.

EYPT.dossier_note:
FIRED, verified three ways. EyePoint's 2026-08-17 release (globenewswire + investors.eyepoint.bio; 8-K accession 0001193125-26-353308), Reuters 2026-08-17 ("EyePoint's eye drug misses main goal in late-stage trial"), and the tape ($14.75 on 08-14 to $4.87 on 08-25, -67%) all agree: LUGANO did not meet the prespecified primary. The board's date (2026-07-31) was already wrong pre-fire by 17 days.

WHY THE $37.50 CANNOT BE REPRODUCED. It was RBC's pre-readout target, withdrawn 2026-08-18 (cut to $5, downgrade to Sector Perform). Same-day broker resets: Chardan $65->$5, Jefferies $30->$8, Jones $43->$20, Citi ->$17, JPMorgan ->Neutral (pre-miss Street average was $38.58). The board's target had no independent derivation behind it — it was a single withdrawn sell-side print.

WIN LEG = $17.00 (LUCIA-conditional, NOT a mark on the fired event). The surviving post-cut targets ($5/$5/$8/$17/$20) are blended numbers that already carry LUCIA risk; a clean LUCIA primary win should clear the top of that band but stays far below $37.50 because one-win/one-miss on the prespecified endpoint is a materially weaker NDA than two wins, and the July-2024 cGMP Warning Letter on the Watertown YUTIQ line sits on the CMC path for a company whose only asset is a manufactured drug-eluting insert (nuance vs the board skeptic: the 10-Q states the required corrective and preventive action plan was FULLY EXECUTED, so this is an overhang, not a confirmed open deficiency). $17.00 = Citi's post-cut mark, below Jones' $20; deliberately taken as the conservative end.

LOSE LEG = $1.75, from the balance sheet, not assertion. 6/30/26 (10-Q filed 2026-08-05): cash + ST investments $180.472m, ZERO borrowed debt, $22.367m finance-lease obligations, payables + accrued $39.3m, equity $166.4m, 83.84m shares out. July ATM added ~1,208,718 shares (~$17m; corroborated — Q2 ATM was 1,429,047 sh at $14.16 wtd avg = $20.2m gross, matching Q2 cash-flow common stock issuance of $20.178m). Realized burn: Q1 op CF -$80.5m, Q2 -$62.3m = $142.9m in H1, roughly $71m/quarter. Carrying to a 12/31/26 readout: $180.5m + $17m - ~$105m (two tapering quarters) = ~$92m, less $22.4m leases = ~$70m net, over ~85m shares = ~$0.82/share of hard net cash. Adding residual DME optionality (COMO/CAPRI fully enrolled, 480+ patients, topline Q4 2027) and YUTIQ gets a busted-single-asset clearing price of $1.50-2.00; I take $1.75.

RUNWAY DISCREPANCY WORTH THE CRO'S ATTENTION. The company guides $180m as runway "into Q4 2027," which implies about $33m/quarter — less than HALF the realized H1 2026 rate of ~$71m/quarter. At the realized rate $180m is ~2.5 quarters (into roughly Q1 2027). The guided runway therefore requires a >50% spend taper or further ATM issuance, and the ATM is already routine — the next tranche prints near a third of the $14.16/$14.44 levels at which the last two were sold.

WIN_PROB 0.30. LUCIA is the same molecule, same insert, same comparator, same endpoint. The bull case is that LUGANO's miss was an artifact of 9 of 211 DURAVYU patients losing 15+ letters "unrelated to wet AMD." But 9/211 versus 0/211 in control is not a chance imbalance (Fisher exact approx. p=0.004 two-sided) — the likelier reading is drug- or device-related, which recurs in an identically designed trial. That is the single strongest reason 0.60 cannot carry over.

EV CHECK, for transparency only (sizing is the Director's): 0.30 x $17.00 + 0.70 x $1.75 = $5.10 + $1.23 = $6.33 against $4.87 spot. Positive on paper — but attached to an UNDATED event, unhedged, with a dilutive raise standing in front of it. catalyst_live=false is the operative field here; these axes exist so the seat is not adjudicated off a dead $37.50/$5.50 pair.

TAKEOUT LENS — NO LIFT APPLIED. The 2026 record-pace biotech M&A cohort (37 takeouts >=$1B YTD, $216B) is late-stage, commercially-ready assets; a failed prespecified primary disqualifies EYPT from that cohort today, so strategic scarcity is currently negative, not positive. The retina precedent that would frame a conditional bid is Astellas/Iveric Bio ($5.9B, April 2023) — but it is three years stale and was a clean pre-approval asset, so it does not carry provenance strong enough to lift the win leg, and I have not lifted it. Any takeout interest is contingent on a LUCIA win, is undated, and is explicitly NOT treated as a milestone.

REGIME CAVEAT. XBI near a five-year high means market-implied win probabilities are rich and old max-fear floor prints are stale-low. Cutting the other way: $408m cap on $180.5m cash means ~$228m of program value is STILL priced in post-crash, so this is not a capitulation print, and the gap between $4.87 and my $1.75 lose-leg is the honest measure of how much LUCIA optimism the tape is already carrying.

LZM.dated_milestone: One real calendar item and one real deadline, neither of which is the catalyst itself. (1) First-half 2026 interim financial results on 29 July 2026, with an investor webcast at 10:00 a.m. New York time hosted by chief executive Chris Showalter and chief financial officer Ingo Hofmaier -- confirmed by the company on 27 July 2026 and verified today. This is a disclosure venue at which management must either produce the concluded process or explain a second missed milestone; it resolves nothing by itself. (2) The Taurus senior secured bridge matures on 31 July 2027, which is the outer bound on how long this can drift -- a deadline that works for the lender, not the shareholder. The catalyst proper -- the strategic-partner transaction -- has no announced date, and the two gates behind it, the Framework Agreement amendment with the Tanzanian government and the power supply agreements, are undated as well.

LZM.dossier_note:
This is a real event on a broken clock, and the discipline that makes this funnel work is the discipline to say so.

Start with what is true. Kabanga is a genuine tier-one orebody -- among the largest and highest-grade development-ready nickel sulfide deposits anywhere, in the cheapest quarter of the cost curve, with an independently prepared study value of $1.58 billion against a $298 million company. The sale process is real, competitive and advanced, corroborated by a wire-service leak specific enough that the company had to respond on 8 June 2026. If it concludes at a defensible fraction of study value, $7.00 is a defensible number and this roughly doubles.

Now what is not true. This is not a defined-risk event position, and treating it as one is the error the catalyst discipline exists to prevent. There is no date: the guided mid-2026 build decision lapsed silently, and 'concluding shortly' was said eighty-nine days ago. There is nothing binding: no agreement, no outside date, no regulator on a clock, no contractual payout. Two hard prerequisites -- a sovereign fiscal amendment and a utility power agreement -- are themselves undated, and one of them cannot be scheduled by anybody. And the floor our board carried at $2.60 is folklore. DDL.thesis_summary: Dingdong agreed on 5 Feb 2026 to sell its China business to Meituan (Two Hearts Investments) for US$717m, with no financing contingency. Shareholders approved it on 27 Mar 2026. The one remaining regulatory gate is SAMR anti-monopoly clearance, which has not come, and the proceeds are then returned to holders. As of 30 Sep 2026 the deal is still pending: the newest EDGAR filing is a director's Form 3 on 16 Sep, the last 6-K is the 21 Aug Q2 release saying the deal awaits SAMR, and there is no press report of clearance, conditions, withdrawal or repricing. The stock trades at $2.18 against a verified US$267.1m of cash held outside the sale perimeter (about $1.13 per ADS), which puts a floor under the break case. The event-win value is about $3.20 per ADS on 236.2m ADS after a leakage reserve and non-controlling interests (NCI). The break value is about $1.65. That is roughly 1.9:1, not the ~2.56:1 the board shows.
DDL.kill_risk: SAMR clearance never comes, or comes with conditions Meituan will not accept, before the ~5 Feb 2027 end date (which can be extended). If the SPA lapses without a refusal, no fee is paid. If Dingdong fails a controllable condition (overseas carve-out, non-resident indirect-transfer tax filing), Dingdong itself owes the US$75m fee (about -$0.32/ADS). The stock then reprices to a China-ADR stub near the $1.65 52-week low, or toward $1.13 of cash in a hard tail. A second leg: net-cash and working-capital price adjustments plus leakage after the US$280m sweep could shave the US$717m. I reserved US$25m for this, but the size is not disclosed.

DDL.dossier_note: Live checks on 30 Sep 2026: FMP quote $2.18. FMP market cap of US$472m implies the 216.6m undiluted denominator; on 236.2m ADS it is about US$515m. FMP/EDGAR filings since 1 Aug: only the 21 Aug Q2 6-K and a 16 Sep Form 3. News since 15 Aug: only the Q2 release and generic comparison pieces. Web search: nothing on SAMR clearance, conditions or withdrawal. The catalyst is real, binding, idiosyncratic and unfired. PENDING_HARD rests on the contractual end date (~2027-02-05, extendable by mutual consent). The resolving act, SAMR clearance, has no date, and an extension would turn this into SLIPPED. Other unannounced closing items: the Buyer's NDRC filing, the overseas carve-out and the non-resident indirect-transfer tax filings. The price is adjustable for net cash, net working capital and leakage. Arithmetic, win case: 717 + 267.1 - 60.6 (tax/costs) - 45.5 (burn) - 75.8 (90% return and stub discount) = 802; less 25 (adjustment/leakage reserve) and 20.7 (redeemable NCI) = 756 / 236.23m ADS = $3.20. Break case: $1.13 cash per ADS plus a $0.40-0.60 stub gives about $1.65 (range $1.50-1.80); the fee's expected value is about 0 because it runs both ways. Upside +47% vs downside -24% from $2.18, about 1.9:1. The Q2 China profit is inflated by RMB199.1m of depreciation suspended under held-for-sale accounting, and interim profit goes to the Buyer, so it does not support the break stub. Not a bio/pharma name and not commodity-linked, so the takeout lens and deck-mark gate do not apply. THRM.dated_milestone: Verified: United States antitrust review completed with early termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period granted at 11:25 a.m. Eastern Time on 26 March 2026; international regulatory clearance also secured. Financing committed at $800 million, with a $550 million five-year revolving credit facility signed 29 June 2026. Registration statement filed 2 July 2026. Closing guided by management on the 23 July 2026 earnings call to early in the fourth quarter of 2026, which is a guided window and not a fixed date. The shareholder special meeting has no announced date and cannot be scheduled until the registration statement is declared effective. A private tax ruling from the Internal Revenue Service remains outstanding.

THRM.dossier_note:
Pass for now. The reason is not that the business is bad or the deal is broken. Both are in reasonable shape. The reason is that we are being asked to buy an event that has already happened, at a price that reflects it.

Our board holds Gentherm as a merger arbitrage gated on United States antitrust risk. That description does not survive contact with the record. The antitrust waiting period was terminated early on 26 March 2026, four months ago, and international clearance is also in hand. Nor was this ever an arbitrage: Gentherm is the acquirer in a Reverse Morris Trust, issuing about 20.7 million of its own shares to absorb Modine's Performance Technologies business. Its shareholders receive no fixed consideration, no exchange ratio protection and no break fee. There is no contractual price to converge to, which means there is no spread and never was one.

The arithmetic is decisive. Our entry's recorded reward-to-risk of 2.87 implies a cost basis near $33.60. Against a $44 target and a $30 floor, that is about 5% of upside against about 29% of downside, a ratio near 0.16 to 1. Reconciling the favourable case of roughly $52 per share against the adverse case of roughly $30 gives a probability-weighted value of about $43 per share, which is 2.7% above the current price. LBTYK.thesis_summary: Liberty Global is a holding company trading at ~$10.64 (LBTYK, ~341m shares, ~$3.63bn market cap) whose resolving event is the spin-off of Ziggo Group — VodafoneZiggo (Netherlands) plus Telenet (Belgium), 13m customers, EUR6.6bn revenue — to be listed on Euronext Amsterdam in 2027, with Liberty Global distributing its 90% to shareholders tax-free for US holders. The structural precondition is now DONE: on 3 August 2026 the company completed the purchase of Vodafone's 50% of VodafoneZiggo for EUR1.0bn cash plus a 10% Ziggo Group stake, so there is no longer a JV partner, no approval contingency and no financing condition standing between here and the listing. The trade is the holdco discount closing: on management's own Q2 marks, guided year-end corporate cash of ~$2.0bn ($5.87/sh) plus the Liberty Growth portfolio at $2.9bn FMV ($8.50/sh) equals $14.37/sh with every telecom asset — 90% of Ziggo Group, 50% of Virgin Media O2, VM Ireland — carried at zero. The listing is the mechanism that forces the market to mark the telecom stub, exactly as the 2024 Sunrise spin did. It is genuinely idiosyncratic: nothing about the outcome depends on the tape, only on whether Liberty Global executes a distribution it has already restructured itself to make. What it is NOT is dated. There is no record date, no listing prospectus, no scheduled shareholder vote; guidance was tightened to "as early as mid-2027" in the 24 July Q2 release and then restated as plain "2027" in the 3 August completion release, and the board retains the right to abandon.
LBTYK.kill_risk: The most load-bearing claim in the thesis is that ~$2.0bn of holdco cash underwrites the downside. It is a forecast, not a balance, and I cannot bridge it from the live record. The Q2 10-Q reconciles exactly to the skeptic's read: consolidated cash $2,418.6m at 30 June 2026, of which only $1,610.1m "represented available liquidity at the corporate level" and $808.5m sits inside the Telenet and VM Ireland borrowing groups. The EUR1.0bn (~$1.15bn) Vodafone payment went out on 3 August, leaving roughly $0.46bn of corporate cash plus $76m of separately-managed-account investments. Getting to $2.0bn by 31 December therefore needs ~$1.5bn of further H2 inflows, and the disposals named to supply it — the 50% Wyre stake (guided only to year-end 2026 or Q1 2027), the VodafoneZiggo towers, Belgian and Dutch property, EUR1.2-1.4bn in total — are described in the company's own 3 August release as proceeds that "will be used to retire debt" at the subsidiaries, not upstreamed to the holding company. I could not determine from any primary source whether the Vodafone payment was funded from holdco cash or from the new Benelux debt (Wyre drew EUR2.71bn of a EUR4.35bn facility, upstreaming ~EUR2.38bn to Telenet, which then repaid EUR2.12bn of its own 2028 maturities); the two readings differ by more than a dollar a share on the floor. Compounding it: ~$340m of the $1.2bn of year-to-date "monetizations" is an asset-backed loan secured on the Wyre stake — borrowed money encumbering the very asset the next checkpoint depends on selling — and the 10-Q states no repurchase program is authorized for 2026, so there is no company bid to defend the discount before the spin. Second-order but real: the resolving event carries no binding date and the 3 August release dropped the "as early as mid-2027" qualifier the Q2 release had added, which is the shape a quiet slip takes before it is announced as one.

LBTYK.dossier_note:
CATALYST. Real, live, unfired, idiosyncratic, and materially de-risked since the board dossier was written. The 3 August 2026 completion of the VodafoneZiggo buyout (EUR1.0bn cash + 10% stake to Vodafone; Liberty Global at 90%) removes the last structural contingency: no JV partner, no pending approval, no financing condition. It is also not a slip - the dossier expected close "by 31 July", it landed 3 August. Not FIRED, because the buyout is preparatory; the resolving event is the distribution and Euronext Amsterdam listing of Ziggo Group, which has not happened. PENDING_SOFT rather than PENDING_HARD because nothing binds the date: the 24 July Q2 release said "the planned Ziggo Group spin-off as early as mid-2027", the 3 August release says only "list Ziggo Group in Amsterdam in 2027", and there is no record date, no prospectus and no scheduled vote. I set dated_milestone to null rather than carry the board's 2027-06-30, which was an invented mid-2027 proxy. The real dated waypoints, none of which resolve the trade: Stephen van Rooyen (CEO) and Jany Fruytier (CFO) take office 1 September 2026 with the rest of the leadership team named that month; the 50% Wyre stake sale guided to year-end 2026 or Q1 2027; EUR1.2-1.4bn of Belgian and Dutch disposals under way.

VALUATION - SoP, ~341m shares ($3.63bn market cap / $10.64). Three stacks, because the difference between them is the whole argument.

(1) Guided stack, which is where the board's $18 lives. Year-end-2026 corporate cash target ~$2.0bn = $5.87/sh, plus Liberty Growth at its Q2 FMV of $2.9bn = $8.50/sh, totals $14.37/sh with 90% of Ziggo Group, 50% of VMO2 and VM Ireland all carried at zero. This reconciles to management's own Q2 statement that cash plus growth marks exceed the share price by about 30% ($4.9bn vs $3.63bn = +35%). The board's $18 implies $6.14bn, i.e. $1.24bn or $3.64/sh for the entire telecom portfolio - roughly 0.2x revenue for the Ziggo equity alone against EUR6.6bn of revenue and ~EUR2.5bn of combined EBITDA. On that basis $18 is reproducible and, if anything, undemanding, so I keep it.

(2) Hard marks today, which the board number quietly assumes away. Corporate-level liquidity was $1,610.1m at 30 June (the 10-Q is explicit that only this slice is available at the corporate level; $808.5m of the $2,418.6m consolidated sits trapped in the Telenet and VM Ireland borrowing groups, and Liberty Global standalone held $0). Less the ~$1.15bn Vodafone payment made 3 August, plus $76m of separately-managed accounts, that is ~$0.54bn = $1.57/sh. Add Growth at full FMV and the stack is $3.44bn = $10.09/sh - approximately the share price. So the "HoldCo cash alone is 60% of market cap" framing circulating in sell-side and Seeking Alpha notes is a forward-dated claim, not a present balance. The bridge from $0.46bn to $2.0bn needs ~$1.5bn of H2 inflows from disposals the company's own 3 August release earmarks for retiring SUBSIDIARY debt.

(3) Floor. $0.46bn cash + $0.08bn SMA + Growth at a 25% haircut ($2.175bn) = $2.715bn = $7.96/sh, telecom at zero. At a 50% haircut it is $5.60/sh. The observed max-fear print is the 27 July close of $9.59 against a 52-week low of $9.30 - and note that low was set AFTER the spin was announced and after the cash target was raised, so it is not a stale pre-catalyst print. I set the floor at $7.50: below the 25%-haircut asset mark, above the punitive case, and materially below the board's $9.50, which was a chart level credited with guided cash. R:R at $10.64 falls from 6.45 to 2.34.

NOT APPLICABLE. Deck-mark gate: no commodity linkage, no feasibility study or price deck - the SoP rests on holdco cash, a venture portfolio marked to FMV, and levered European cable equity. Takeout lens: not a bio/pharma name; the 2026 biotech M&A regime is irrelevant here and I have not imported any takeout optionality into the target.

SKEPTIC PASS ON MYSELF. The claim I leaned hardest on is that cash and marks underwrite the downside. Attacked from the live record, it does not hold as stated - see kill_risk. Two further quality problems I could not clear: ~$340m of the $1.2bn of "monetizations" is an asset-backed loan against the Wyre stake, so leverage on the asset the next checkpoint depends on selling is being counted as cash raised; and the 10-Q states no share repurchase program is authorized for 2026, so no company bid exists to close the discount before the listing. Unresolved fact I flag rather than guess: I could not establish from any primary source whether the EUR1.0bn Vodafone payment was funded from holdco cash or from the new Benelux debt (Wyre drew EUR2.71bn of a EUR4.35bn facility, upstreaming ~EUR2.38bn to Telenet, which repaid EUR2.12bn of 2028 maturities). If it came from the Benelux structure, the floor is roughly a dollar-plus per share higher than I have marked it and the $2.0bn bridge is far less strained. VIR.thesis_summary: Held seat into a dated, unfired, idiosyncratic Phase 3 readout: ECLIPSE 1 topline (TND + ALT normalisation at week 48 vs a deferred-treatment control, n=124) guided for Q4 2026 and restated in the 5 Aug 2026 8-K with nothing on file since. The control arm is untreated, so the statistical bar is low relative to SOLSTICE's 66% undetectable / 56% composite at week 48; the real question is the magnitude of the strict TND+ALT composite versus daily bulevirtide (FDA accelerated approval 22 May 2026), which now anchors the commercial case. Balance sheet is cash-backed ($1.01B at 30 Jun 2026, no debt, runway into 2H 2028, Astellas $240M upfront + $75M equity at $10.36 already banked), so the lose leg is a cash-plus-partnered-oncology floor rather than a zero. Binary legs at $10.65: win $21, lose $4.25, p(win) 0.70; EV about $16, R:R about 1.6:1, market-implied p about 38%.
VIR.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is a ~70% clean win on the strict TND+ALT composite. Refutation from the live record: SOLSTICE's 56% composite used a looser definition (undetectable OR >=2-log drop, plus ALT normalisation); the strict ECLIPSE 1 composite (TND plus ALT normalisation) is plausibly ~40-50%, and ALT normalisation is the noisy component (only 56% normalised ALT at week 48 in SOLSTICE; HBsAg-lowering agents produce ALT excursions). A print near 40% would still beat an untreated arm at p<0.05 but would read as optical parity with bulevirtide's MYR301 composite (45-48%), handing the market the 'stat win, commercial miss' middle outcome in which the stock drifts toward the lose leg despite a technically positive trial. Timing residual: the registry primary-completion date (31 Dec 2026, unchanged since 8 Apr 2026) is the last day of the guided quarter and the company's own Nov 2025 guidance said Q1 2027, so a slip to Jan-Feb 2027 is documented and live. Minor: five Form 144s (21 Aug-17 Sep 2026) show insiders selling into the run.

Prosus's stated position, from its 16 July 2026 announcement, is that the sale to Uber is a fair price and an effective way to comply; whether the Commission formally accepts a settlement that completes in 2027 against a 2026 deadline is the one genuinely open item, and its downside is a small residual placement, not a re-rating. MP.dated_milestone: Two dates are real and verified, and neither is a payout. 6 August 2026, after the US close: second-quarter 2026 results and webcast, confirmed by the company on 16 July 2026. There is no deal to close, no regulatory decision on MP itself, no spin, no forced seller clearing, no activist. OLMA.thesis_summary: Olema Pharmaceuticals (OLMA, $8.54, 30 Sep 2026). Binary on OPERA-01, the pivotal Phase 3 of palazestrant monotherapy vs investigator-choice endocrine therapy in 2L/3L ER+/HER2- mBC after CDK4/6i, primary = BICR PFS analysed separately in ESR1-mutant and ESR1-wild-type cohorts (n~510). Enrollment complete; top-line guided to Q1 2027 (10 Aug 2026 8-K/PR), restated unchanged at Citi 10 Sep, Morgan Stanley 15 Sep and H.C. Wainwright 16 Sep ("fully enrolled", "data-maturation phase"). Registry NCT06016738 unchanged since 13 Aug: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, est. primary completion 31 Oct 2026. Unfired: EDGAR shows nothing after a Form 4 on 2 Sep 2026. Stock re-rated from the board's $11.32 to $8.54 (year low $6.65) after AstraZeneca's SERENA-4 miss on 11 Sep 2026 (second 1L oral-SERD combo failure of 2026 after persevERA) - a class read-through, not an OLMA fact; OPERA-01 is a different setting (2L monotherapy, CDK4/6i-pretreated, ESR1-stratified) where oral SERDs have hit in ESR1m (EMERALD, EMBER-3, SERENA-6) and never in ESR1wt. The wt cohort is the coin-flip; the ESR1m cohort is the likely partial-win. Three-branch: full win (both cohorts) $28, partial (ESR1m only) ~$7, miss ~$2.1.
OLMA.dated_milestone: OPERA-01 pivotal Phase 3 top-line (palazestrant monotherapy vs investigator-choice endocrine therapy, 2L/3L ER+/HER2- mBC post-CDK4/6i; primary = BICR PFS analysed separately in ESR1-mutant and ESR1-wild-type cohorts; n~510). Company guidance: first quarter of 2027 - Q2-2026 release/8-K Ex.99.1, 10 Aug 2026: "Completed enrollment in the pivotal Phase 3 OPERA-01 trial; top-line data are now expected in the first quarter of 2027" (one slip from fall-2026 guided 16 Mar 2026). OLMA.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the ESR1-wild-type cohort is a genuine ~45% coin-flip rather than a likely miss. The refutation from the record: no oral SERD has ever shown a PFS benefit in ESR1wt (EMERALD wt no benefit; EMBER-3 ITT HR 0.87 n.s.; persevERA and SERENA-4 both missed in unselected 1L). Palazestrant's wt evidence is a single-arm Phase 2 mPFS of 5.5 months - which is numerically the same as the EMBER-3 standard-of-care ITT arm (5.5 months). The defence is that OPERA-01 requires prior CDK4/6i, where fulvestrant/AI controls run ~2-3.5 months (EMERALD control 1.9 months), so 5.5 would clear; but that comparison is cross-trial and single-arm. If wt misses, the outcome is the partial branch (~$7, ESR1m-only label competing with Orserdu and Lilly's approved Inluriyo), which the market already discounts. Residual: the full-win $28 leg carries ~30% weight and 70% of outcomes sit at or below the current $8.54. Also live: TD Cowen ATM (~$158m of $200m cap unused) will sell into any pre-readout rally, and the accrued-R&D/secured-loan structure means the cash floor prints below gross cash (see note).

Natural acquirer is Novartis (equity holder via the $250m private placement, ribociclib supply/collab in OPERA-02); Lilly already owns Inluriyo. XBI-high caveat does not apply here: OLMA trades near its low, and the market-implied win probability has fallen, not risen.

DBVT.thesis_summary: DBV filed the BLA for the VIASKIN Peanut patch in children aged 4-7 on 29 Sep 2026 (GlobeNewswire release plus an 8-K accepted 29 Sep, on the last day of the guided quarter). The filing rests on the Phase 3 VITESSE trial: 654 children, 46.6% responders on the patch vs 14.8% on placebo, clearing the FDA's 15% lower-bound bar. The product has Breakthrough Therapy designation and DBV has asked for Priority Review. The next event that binds the FDA is its day-60 decision on whether to accept the filing, due about 28 Nov 2026. The PDUFA date should be set in the day-74 letter, about mid-Dec 2026. The approval decision itself falls about 29 May 2027 under priority review or about 29 Sep 2027 under standard review. The only other approved peanut immunotherapy, Palforzia, was withdrawn worldwide on 31 Jul 2026, so an approved patch would be the only approved peanut desensitisation product in the US for this age group. Per-ADS values here are computed on the fully diluted base of about 91.4M ADS, not the 62.9M the board used.
DBVT.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the filing is clean and approvable once VITESSE met its endpoint. Refutation attempt: the Q2-26 10-Q lists as a risk whether DBV's sole contract manufacturer of the VIASKIN patch can fix the GMP deficiencies FDA cited in warning letters. That is a site-level route to refusal-to-file, a CRL, or a delayed pre-approval inspection, and it is independent of the efficacy data. DBV has also had a CRL on this patch before (2020, adhesion and manufacturing-related). Dilution is a second-order risk: about $17M/month burn, cash runway into Q3 2027 (around the standard-review date), and an open $150M ATM already used for $50M to RA Capital on 30 Jul. Expect more issuance before the decision. Priority Review is requested, not granted. A standard review pushes the decision to about Sep 2027, at the edge of the cash runway.

KDP.thesis_summary: KDP is separating its coffee business (Global Coffee Co., which includes US Coffee plus the JDE Peet's assets acquired 1 Apr 2026 for $18.4B) from the North American refreshment-beverage business via a tax-free spin-off targeted for "early 2027" — reaffirmed in the Q2 release of 6 Aug 2026 and the 10-Q of 10 Aug 2026. The trade in KDP common is a sum-of-the-parts re-rating on completion, NOT an index-flow trade: KDP is the RemainCo, retains the ticker, listing and index seat, and index funds are obliged to keep these shares. Whatever forced flow the transaction creates lands on the SpinCo, a security that does not yet exist. The parts are genuinely mismatched — a ~30%-margin US beverage franchise growing sales 10.0% and segment OI 11.9% sits inside the same multiple as a coffee arm whose adjusted OI fell 24.7% y/y on green-coffee costs and tariffs — and the blended entity trades at ~10.6x 2027E EBITDA against parts worth ~11.5-12x. The event itself is real and unfired but carries no binding date, no Form 10 on file as of 25 Aug 2026, no board approval of the distribution, and the company's own stated conditions include "appropriate leverage levels at each company, and supportive market conditions."
KDP.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that completion unlocks an unpaid-for SoP re-rating. Three live facts cut against it. (1) The parts are largely already paid for: sell-side consensus PT is $37.75 (median $38, high $42) versus my $38.50, so the SoP is the consensus view, not a variant one — and the stock is already +12.6% over its 200d MA and 3.9% off its 52-week high, so the discount has been narrowing without the event. (2) The company conditions separation timing on "supportive market conditions" and on reaching appropriate leverage at each entity — by its own language the event is tape-dependent, not idiosyncratic, which is disqualifying for an event-driven sleeve; a risk-off tape both delays the catalyst and de-rates the stock at the same time (correlated, not independent). (3) Execution wobble is real and unresolved: no Form 10 on file at 25 Aug 2026 (a US distribution cannot occur until one is filed and effective, normally 2-4 months ahead), the board has not approved the distribution, and the designated Global Coffee CEO left at end-July 2026 with no successor named — the SpinCo has no CEO roughly five months from its own target window. Secondary: my CoffeeCo leg at 9.5x may itself be generous — US Coffee adjusted OI is running −24.7% y/y and a standalone, levered coffee company carrying green-coffee and tariff cost pass-through could clear at 8x or less, which alone removes ~$2/sh from the target.

BLCO.dossier_note: Wait for this one, and be specific about what you are waiting for. This funnel exists to buy defined-risk asymmetry around a scheduled event, and on those terms Bausch + Lomb does not qualify today. The catalyst is a soft, non-binding intention rather than a firm, scheduled event, and it has been soft for six years running: stated in August 2020, restated at the 2022 listing, restated in August 2022, unblocked by the April 2024 patent ruling, taken to market in autumn 2024, and abandoned on 6 February 2025 with the words 'that process is complete, and will not result in a transaction at this time.' Then, in April 2025, the parent refinanced $7.9 billion and pushed its 2025-2028 maturities out to 2031 and 2032. That is the single fact that should govern this decision: the pressure that would have forced the sale has been removed, and the parent's chief financial officer now dates the decision to cash generated through the end of 2027. A seller with five more years of runway is not a forced seller, which means the forced-seller premise on our board entry is no longer accurate. Two legal gates make it worse rather than better - a distribution needs an independent solvency opinion on a roughly $21 billion debt load, and a New Jersey court has allowed fraudulent-transfer claims to proceed that expressly include the right to block a dividend of these very shares, with the plaintiffs free to renew their injunction motion the moment the parent moves. The floor is the second problem.

CELC.dossier_note: This seat existed for one reason: a dated regulatory decision with a spread between the live price and the value the decision would unlock. That decision fired on 14 July 2026, three days early, and it went our way. The position is nonetheless down about 46% from the high. That single fact settles the question this funnel is meant to answer. The discipline here is not to be clever about it. A catalyst that has already resolved is spent, whichever way it resolved. The asymmetry we were paid to underwrite - a hard date, a binding decision, a bounded loss - no longer exists in this name. What remains is a commercial-launch story: whether a first-time commercial company can ship on time, whether oncologists will accept a regimen that produced mouth sores in 58 to 72% of trial patients, and whether a second label arrives before the competition does. Those are perfectly respectable questions. They are not event-driven questions, and they cannot be answered before the first revenue line arrives in early November 2026. The second finding is the one that decides the sizing. The downside floor of $60 carried on the board is not a floor. It is a bear valuation that already assumes the launch broadly works - at $60 the enterprise is worth about $2.79B, which needs peak annual sales above $1.2B. The only hard number underneath is net cash of roughly $140M, about $3 a share. There is no acquirer under contract, no contingent payment right, no recovery value. A defensible adverse case is $5

AQST.thesis_summary: Anaphylm (oral sublingual epinephrine) is on a post-CRL repair path: the Jan-30-2026 CRL deficiencies (human factors, packaging, one supportive PK study) were addressed with clean topline results announced 8/10/26 (pouch-open 17s to 3s, placement errors down >80%, self-admin PK comparable), and management reaffirmed on 8/11 an NDA resubmission on or before 9/30/26. The resubmission is company-controlled and NOT yet filed as of 8/25 (EDGAR through 8/18: only Forms 4 after the 8/10-8/11 disclosures), so no FDA action date exists; a Class 2 classification (new clinical data) implies a six-month review and a decision ~Mar-Apr 2027 on a 9/30 filing. Approval by 2027-06-30 unlocks ~$95M contingent, non-dilutive funding ($75M RTW purchase, $20M Oaktree Tranche B). The edge case has compressed: at 4.80 (8/24 close, $602M mcap) AQST trades ABOVE the approved-and-launched needle-free comp ARS Pharmaceuticals/SPRY (5.35, $531M, ~$117M TTM revenue), so the market-implied win probability is already rich.
AQST.kill_risk: The catalyst is still self-declared: five weeks before the guided 9/30 deadline no resubmission has been filed, and the FDA cannot start a clock on an unfiled application. The new PK and HF studies make Class 2 (six-month review) the likely classification — management itself concedes expedited review cannot be guaranteed — so any slip of the filing into Q4 pushes the decision into Q2-2027, up against the 2027-06-30 RTW/Oaktree approval deadlines: the same slip that costs time forfeits ~$95M of non-dilutive funding on a balance sheet with a $56.6M stockholders' deficit and ~$89M of pre-sold revenue/royalty claims senior to the equity. Meanwhile the price already exceeds the approved comp (SPRY $531M), so even a clean approval may deliver little upside versus the comp-marked win leg (~$5.00).

If approved it is the first therapy for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The event is genuinely idiosyncratic (resolves on FDA action, not the tape) and unfired at 80 days out. Critically, though, this is NOT a single-asset binary: BBIO is a $14.7B commercial-stage company whose value is dominated by the acoramidis/Attruby ATTR-CM franchise (Q2-26 US net product revenue $222.4M, +211% YoY; total revenue $243.7M; $1B+ global 2026 guidance), with two further NDAs pending (encaleret PDUFA 2027-05-08; infigratinib submitted Q3-26). Over the 80-day window the P&L will be dominated by Attruby quarterly prints, the Aug-31 US-government MFN/Medicaid pricing agreement flowing through net price, KKR/Frazier supply overhang (5.0M-share secondary priced 2026-08-14; Frazier cut its stake 55% in Q2), and the biotech tape — NOT by the PDUFA. WBD.thesis_summary: Paramount Skydance is acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery for $31.00/share ALL CASH ($81B equity, ~$110B EV incl. ticking fee); WBD holders approved, DOJ cleared, and the European Commission formally cleared on 2026-07-22. The sole remaining gate is a 12-state antitrust suit before Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin (N.D. Cal.), which has stopped the deal cold: a TRO was granted 2026-07-20 and extended, and on 2026-07-24 Paramount STIPULATED it will not consummate until the earlier of a merits ruling or 2027-06-01. Paramount then abandoned the preliminary-injunction stage entirely - its counsel concluded plaintiffs would likely prevail at PI - and cancelled the 2026-08-03 hearing in favour of a speedy merits trial. Trial date is NOT set: Paramount wants November 2026, the states asked for a 12-15 day trial starting 2027-04-05. The event is real, forward-dated, unfired and idiosyncratic (it resolves on a courtroom ruling, not the tape), but it is no longer a dated Q3-2026 convergence - it is a ~10-month legal binary with a ticking-fee carry of only ~$0.25/share/quarter starting 2026-09-30.
WBD.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim in the thesis is the cushioned break leg: that a blocked deal pays WBD the $7B reverse-termination fee (+$2.79/sh), holding the floor near $17. Two live refutations. (1) The RTF is payable only on a REGULATORY termination as defined in the merger agreement; a negotiated walk-away, a Paramount financing failure (Larry Ellison personally guaranteed $40.4B, collateral tied to Oracle stock), or a mutual termination on other grounds may not trigger it - the floor then collapses toward the naked standalone $12-17. (2) More probable and priced by neither of my legs: with a ~1-year delay, Paramount's own concession that it would lose the PI, and $9.8B of total Ellison break exposure, the realistic middle path is a RENEGOTIATED LOWER price or a restructured deal (e.g. carving out the assets the states object to), not a clean $31.75 vs $17.00 binary. A cut to, say, $27-28 leaves the buyer at ~breakeven against today's $26.09 while I have carried ten months of dead time. Secondary: my 0.55 win_prob sits BELOW the ~0.62 undiscounted market-implied, and the bull rebuttal is strong - state AGs rarely succeed in blocking a merger their federal counterpart has already cleared, and both DOJ and the EC have cleared this one. A second regulatory front is also still open in the UK, where producers and talent are lobbying the culture minister to intervene.

SVRA.thesis_summary: Savara's MOLBREEVI (inhaled molgramostim) BLA in autoimmune PAP is under FDA Priority Review with a binding PDUFA target action date of 22 November 2026 (53 days out), no advisory committee, and a Phase 3 (IMPALA-2, NEJM) that met its primary DLco endpoint. The event is idiosyncratic and unfired: approval triggers ~$150M of non-dilutive capital (RTW $75M royalty + Hercules $75M tranche) and a 2027 US launch into ~5,500 diagnosed patients; a CRL would most likely be CMC-driven (the file was refused on CMC in May 2025 and took a major amendment in April 2026). Binary axes: win ~$9, lose ~$2.25, p(win) ~0.70 vs a market-implied ~0.42 at $5.08.
SVRA.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is p(approval)=0.70 with CMC as the only live hazard. The live record cannot confirm the FDA has inspected and cleared the third-party manufacturing site: the Q2 release and 10-Q are silent on pre-approval inspection, the April 2026 major amendment arose from FDA information requests two months into a review that had already been refused once on CMC, and there has been no 8-K since 11 August. At my axes the tape prices only ~42% (and ~49% even at the board's $8/$2.50), a 20-28 point gap that either reflects a lower street win leg (launch into a small population with a heavy-dilution history) or genuine CMC doubt; the stock has drifted ~10% lower since 21 September on no news at above-average volume. Residual: a CMC CRL forfeits both $75M approval-gated facilities at once, leaves ~$120M cash (~$0.35/FD share net of Hercules) against ~$31M/quarter burn, and forces a raise near $2; an efficacy-based CRL would settle nearer $1.50. There is no asset-backed floor - $2.25 is a precedent-and-scenario blend, not net cash.

IMXI.thesis_summary: Cash merger arb: Western Union acquires International Money Express for $16.00/share cash (announced 2025-08-11, ~$500M). Shareholder vote passed 2025-12-09; HSR expired 2025-10-06; money-transmission regulators in 51 of 52 US states/territories and every international jurisdiction have cleared. The entire trade now rests on ONE outstanding approval - New York DFS - after which the parties close. Stock at $12.255 vs $16.00 is a 30.6% gross spread, i.e. the market prices roughly a coin-flip on completion, not a normal late-stage arb. Timeline has slipped twice (contractual outside date 2026-05-11 already extended to 2026-08-10, further extension to 2026-11-10 available while regulatory approval is pending); Western Union's 2026-07-30 Q2 guidance now assumes a 2026-09-01 close. The trade is a bet on NYDFS clearing and WU not using the delay to re-cut price against a target whose standalone earnings have collapsed since signing.
IMXI.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "WU still intends to close at $16.00" - and the live record materially weakens it. WU's 2026-07-30 Q2 missed badly (adj EPS $0.31 vs $0.42 est and $0.42 LY, adj operating margin -4pp, Americas retail deteriorating, stock $8.47 on an ~11-13% yield). IMXI itself has deteriorated far more since signing: Q1-26 revenue $121.95M vs $144.31M (-15.5%), net income $0.51M vs $7.77M (-93%), principal sent -11.4%, operating cash flow swung to -$37.4M, revolver drawn $240.8M against a $369M market cap. So WU has both motive and an option point: it can decline to trigger the final outside-date extension on 2026-08-10 and press for a lower price on an asset now worth conspicuously less than at signing. Crucially, the $27.3M reverse fee is payable only under specified ANTITRUST restraints - HSR cleared in Oct-2025 - so a failure driven by a state money-transmitter regulator likely pays IMXI NOTHING; holders eat the full break to standalone value. The NY holdout is also substantive rather than clerical (public consumer-advocacy comment filed against the change-of-control). A persistent 30% spread in a deal with 51 of 52 approvals in hand is the arb community telling you it sees this.

CMCSA.thesis_summary: Comcast announced 2026-06-29 (8-K Ex-99.1) its intention to separate into two public companies via a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal + Sky, "expected to be completed in approximately one year" (i.e. ~mid-2027). RemainCo = domestic broadband/wireless/business services on the 65m-home converged network (Michael Angelakis CEO); SpinCo = Universal parks/studios, NBC/Telemundo, Peacock, Bravo and Sky (Mike Cavanagh CEO). The trade is a sum-of-the-parts re-rate: the consolidated entity trades at ~4.85x EV/EBITDA (EV $169.9B on $87.2B cap + $82.7B Q2-2026 net debt, over ~$35B FY26E adjusted EBITDA), while the live comps are CHTR at 5.70x and DIS at 10.81x EV/EBITDA TTM. Marking the parts at 5.5x / 7.5x on 2027E gets ~$34/sh vs $24.56 spot. Carry is paid by the $0.33/qtr dividend declared 2026-07-23 (5.4% yield, covered ~3.5x by H1-26 FCF of $8.5B).
CMCSA.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "the parts re-rate." Three live facts cut against it. (1) Comcast just ran this experiment: the Versant spin closed 2026-01-02 and the stub went from a $32.86 52-wk high to a $21.28 low - a spin at this issuer has already failed once in seven months to re-rate the remainder. (2) The EBITDA base is eroding faster than the multiple is likely to expand: Q2-26 residential C&P adjusted EBITDA fell 8.0% y/y, domestic broadband revenue -5.5%, 167k broadband subs lost in the quarter, and total adjusted EBITDA fell 5.3% y/y even pro forma for Versant/Sky-Germany. A 23-month hold against a -5%/yr base eats most of a one-turn re-rate. (3) The Disney-multiple analogue is structurally blocked: the 8-K states NBCUniversal will carry "the same dual-class share structure as Comcast" (Roberts control retained) and Comcast keeps up to 19.9% of SpinCo to monetize over time - a governance discount plus a stated overhang, against a single-class DIS comp. Deal risk is also non-trivial and self-declared: final board approval, tax opinions, regulatory approvals and financing are all still outstanding, with "no assurance that the proposed transaction will be completed." Finally, the driver is only semi-idiosyncratic - completion resolves on company facts, but the realized value depends on where the tape chooses to multiple cable and legacy media in mid-2027.

Comcast no longer discloses Sky standalone, so I carry Sky at ~2.8B, down from the ~3.0B last disclosed for FY24 to reflect the Germany disposal. THIS IS THE SOFTEST NUMBER IN THE STACK - every +/-0.5B on Sky moves the target roughly +/-$0.6/sh, and it moves it in opposite directions for the two legs (it shifts EBITDA from a 5.5x bucket to a 7.5x bucket). Step 5, total EV 201.0B, less mid-2027E net debt ~80B (roughly flat: ~14B/yr FCF against ~4.7B dividends and ~4B buybacks, plus separation financing), = equity 121.0B over ~3.50B shares = $34.57. GLUE.thesis_summary: The GFORCE-1 full readout for MRT-8102 is a Phase 1 trial of an oral NLRP3 molecular-glue degrader in people with high cardiovascular risk. It is real, unfired and specific to the company. Monte Rosa guides it only to "H2 2026" (Q2 release, 6 Aug 2026). Enrolment and dosing are complete. Interim data showed an 85% median CRP reduction at 4 weeks, so the result will turn more on the dose-response, how long the effect lasts and safety than on whether the drug works at all. Price is $11.74, about $992M market cap and about 84.5M shares. The $626M of cash at Q2 plus the $50M Novartis milestone for MRT-6160 (paid 8 Sep) comes to roughly $7/share. That leaves little more than $4/share of value on MRT-8102, the Novartis milestone stream and the platform. Re-marked axes: win $21, floor $8.50, p = 0.55.
GLUE.kill_risk: The thesis leans hardest on the claim that a clean full GFORCE-1 dataset re-rates the stock toward about $21. That is weak for three reasons. First, the headline efficacy (85% CRP cut) was already published in the interim, so a confirmatory full readout could be a sell-the-news event. Second, after the Jul-2026 ZEUS failure (HR 0.99, taken from the skeptic record and not re-verified here), investors may discount CRP-lowering as a surrogate for cardiovascular benefit. Third, the timing is a company-controlled window with no date. The Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley conferences in September passed without narrowing it, and the readout could slip into 2027 or come out quietly at a medical meeting. On the downside, cash of about $7/share limits the loss, but a safety signal (liver or infection) in the full dataset would push toward cash value.

IMTX.thesis_summary: Immatics is a binary on anzu-cel (IMA203), a one-time autologous PRAME TCR-T cell therapy, in the randomised Phase 3 SUPRAME trial in previously-treated advanced melanoma (post-PD1), primary endpoint PFS. Phase 1b at RP2D reads 56% cORR / 14.6mo mDOR / 6.1mo mPFS / 16.2mo mOS / 46% 2-yr OS against a physician's-choice control arm that historically delivers ~2-3mo mPFS, so the effect size on offer is large. The resolving event has SLIPPED: 12-May-2026 guidance said pre-specified interim AND final PFS analyses would be triggered in 2026; the 18-Aug-2026 Q2 release replaced both with a single streamlined final analysis at a lower prespecified event count (PFS events accruing slower than modelled), pushing topline to H1-2027 with a BLA in 2027 and no launch before 2028. The only firmly dated event left in the window is ESMO abstract 1955RO on 24-Oct-2026 (first Phase 1b data for the IMA402 PRAME bispecific at RP2D) — real and idiosyncratic, but it does not resolve the binary. On live anchors the trade is a full-price option, not a spread: the win leg re-derives to $14.00 (not the board's $20) and the failure leg to $2.25, giving +61% / -74% from $8.69, an INVERTED 0.82:1 payoff, with market-implied win probability of ~55% already above my blended 45%.
IMTX.dated_milestone: 2026-10-24 — ESMO Congress 2026, Madrid, rapid oral 1955RO, 08:30-10:00 CEST (Schadendorf): first Phase 1b results for IMA402 PRAME TCR bispecific at the RP2D range. This is the ONLY firmly dated, verifiable event and it is NOT the thesis-resolving one. Load-bearing event = SUPRAME Phase 3 PFS topline, guided H1-2027 (undated within a six-month window), BLA 2027; nearest verifiable checkpoint on that path is completion of ~450 randomisations targeted by year-end 2026.
IMTX.kill_risk: My win leg is not an independent valuation — it is a ratio to Iovance, and Iovance's own tape is the weakest link. The $1.75bn filing-stage EV for anzu-cel is set at ~52% of IOVA's live EV of $3.347bn (mkt cap $3.599bn less $251.7m net cash: $297.7m cash+STI, $46.0m leases, 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet). But IOVA closed $8.06 against a 52-week low of $1.76 and a 200-day average of $3.66 — the comp EV is more than double its own 200-day, struck with XBI at 164.17 versus a 52-week low of 88.71, i.e. near a multi-year high. If IOVA mean-reverts toward its 200-day, the anchor EV falls to roughly $1.4bn and my $1.75bn mark for a pre-approval, pre-revenue asset would sit ABOVE the approved incumbent — indefensible — and the win leg compresses to roughly $9-10, which is the current price. So the entire "+61% upside" claim is levered to a comparable trading at a 52-week high in the hottest biotech tape in five years, and the binary would still have three-to-four quarters to run after any comp de-rating. Second, live and specific: the 18-Aug-2026 disclosure that aggregate PFS events are accruing more slowly than modelled forced a re-cut of the analysis to a lower event count. Fewer events means a wider confidence interval on the hazard ratio, and the change was driven by observed data rather than by plan — the company asserts 90% power retained, which is unverifiable from outside. A design amendment made under the data is a genuine statistical-risk flag, not a neutral logistics update. Third, ITT dilution: anzu-cel is autologous, so patients randomised to it who never reach infusion (apheresis, manufacture, lymphodepletion attrition) count against the treatment arm — precisely where single-arm Phase 1b response rates historically fail to translate in this modality.

IMTX.dossier_note:
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-25. Sources: FMP quote/press-release feeds, Immatics Q2-2026 balance sheet and cash-flow statement (filed 18-Aug-2026, CIK 0001809196, EUR reporting currency), Immatics 17-Jul-2026 ESMO announcement, IOVA Q2-2026 balance sheet (filed 06-Aug-2026), live EURUSD 1.16645.

1) CATALYST — REAL, IDIOSYNCRATIC, UNFIRED, BUT SLIPPED. The event layer survives; the timing did not. 12-May-2026: "pre-specified interim and final data analyses are expected to be triggered in 2026." 18-Aug-2026: both replaced by a single streamlined final PFS analysis at a lower prespecified event count, because aggregate PFS events are accruing more slowly than modelled; trial expanded to ~450 patients; topline H1-2027; BLA 2027. FROM 2026 interim + 2026 final -> TO a single H1-2027 final. Registry NCT06743126 carries an estimated primary completion of January 2028, i.e. the registry is looser than the guidance. Nothing here is tape-driven — this resolves on its own trial data. catalyst_live stays true.

2) MILESTONE. The only firmly dated, independently verifiable event is ESMO 24-Oct-2026, 08:30-10:00 CEST, abstract 1955RO, rapid oral, presenter Dirk Schadendorf, "Initial Results with IMA402, a PRAME-Targeted TCR-based Bispecific T-cell Engager in Advanced Solid Tumors" (confirmed against the 17-Jul-2026 company release; ESMO Congress 23-27 Oct 2026, Madrid). DIRECTOR/CRO WARNING: the binary DOES NOT RESOLVE ON 24 OCTOBER. That date prices only the bispecific leg (~$0.25bn of a $2.21bn win-case equity). staging stays TRUE because the load-bearing SUPRAME topline is undated inside a six-month window.

3) VALUATION AXES — binary_prob, both legs corrected, arithmetic shown.
WIN LEG $14.00. Comp verified live rather than asserted: Iovance market cap $3.599bn at $8.06, less net cash of $251.7m ($297.7m cash+short-term investments minus $46.0m lease obligations, 30-Jun-2026) = EV $3.347bn, against FY-2026 guided Amtagvi revenue of $350-370m in the IDENTICAL indication (previously-treated advanced melanoma post-checkpoint) across 95+ authorised treatment centres. Anzu-cel on a clean randomised PFS win is pre-approval, pre-revenue, launch not before 2028, and would take share FROM Amtagvi rather than enter a virgin market — but it earns a real premium to the prior bear mark because a randomised Phase 3 supporting FULL approval is a stronger regulatory position than lifileucel's single-arm accelerated approval, and 56% cORR versus roughly 31% deserves credit. Mark it at $1.75bn, ~52% of the verified incumbent EV. Plus bispecific franchise / IMA203CD8 / Moderna collaboration / discovery engine $0.25bn. Plus residual cash at readout $0.21bn (see below). Equity $2.21bn / ~158m shares = $13.99, carried $14.00. Share bridge: 136.6m today (par value EUR1,366,435 at EUR0.01), ATM drip to ~144m by readout (they took EUR22.1m in Q1-2026 and EUR99.4m in Q4-2025, so the programme is live), then a commercial raise on the win path treated as value-neutral (cash in, consumed by build-out and pre-revenue burn) to ~158m. The raise is now structurally REQUIRED on the win path: runway does not reach first revenue in any outcome.
FAILURE LEG $2.25. EUR393.2m cash+STI at 30-Jun-2026, less four quarters at ~EUR53m (TTM operating outflow EUR206.2m: -61.2 Q2-26, -42.7 Q1-26, -57.6 Q4-25, -44.7 Q3-25, plus ~EUR3.7m capex) = ~EUR183m at a mid-2027 readout = ~$213m, or ~$1.55-1.80 per share on a drifted count. Residual platform on a failure is impaired but not zero at $0.45-0.70. Floor $2.10-2.50, carried $2.25.
WHY $2.25 AND NOT LOWER: the hot-tape caveat cuts in the bull's favour here. XBI is at 164.17 against a 52-week low of 88.71 and within 3% of its high — old max-fear "0.8-1.2x residual net cash" clearing prints for busted biotechs are stale-low in this regime. A second, genuine de-correlation the prior pass missed: IMA402 prints at ESMO in OCTOBER 2026, roughly eight months BEFORE SUPRAME topline. If the bispecific shows real activity in October, the PRAME-target hypothesis is partially validated independently, and the residual leg is no longer purely hostage to the cell-therapy failure. The correlation argument (same antigen, lower-potency modality, therefore impaired on the same day) is directionally right but is largely SETTLED BEFORE the binary resolves, not on it.
CONSEQUENCE. From $8.69: +61.1% to $14.00, -74.1% to $2.25, payoff 0.82:1 — INVERTED. Market-implied win probability = (8.69-2.25)/(14.00-2.25) = 54.8%, at or above my blended 45%. Expected value 0.45 x 14.00 + 0.55 x 2.25 = $7.54, roughly -13% against the traded price BEFORE discounting three to four quarters at a biotech cost of capital. Under the finer frame (35% clean win $14.00, 20% marginal win ~$8.50, 45% failure $2.25) EV is $7.61 — same conclusion. The spread is already gone.

4) TAKEOUT LENS — ASSESSED, NO LIFT TAKEN, AND DELIBERATELY SO. The 2026 regime is real and I found named provenance: Gilead/Arcellx, announced February 2026, ~$7.8bn for anito-cel, a late-stage CAR-T with a US decision due December 2026; J&J/Firefly Bio $1bn; five in-vivo cell-therapy acquisitions totalling over $7.3bn between March 2025 and February 2026. But the lens conditions on "pivotal data IN HAND or near approval," and Immatics is neither — SUPRAME has not read out, and Arcellx carried registrational data plus a Kite partnership when Gilead bid. Anzu-cel post-win would be the only randomised-controlled solid-tumour TCR-T asset in existence, which is genuine strategic scarcity, and plausible acquirers are Gilead (Kite cell-therapy infrastructure, explicitly buying late-stage cell therapy) and Merck & Co (melanoma franchise adjacency). Bristol Myers Squibb is the obvious name and the WEAKEST one: it handed IMA401 back effective 12-Dec-2024, so the large-pharma validation on the bispecific franchise is already gone. Conclusion: the takeout leg is undated optionality that becomes live only AFTER a SUPRAME win, at which point it is embedded in the re-rate — it is not a milestone, it does not extend or substitute for one, and it does not lift $14.00 today. It is, however, where the board's $20 was implicitly coming from; a post-win takeout at a 40-60% premium to standalone reaches $19-22, which is a CONDITIONAL CAP, not fair value.

5) INSTRUMENT NOTE (fact, not a trade view): the board's own instrument line already flags that options carry a full 9-12 month binary IV load. That was written when the binary was expected to resolve in 2026; after the slip the option path now spans roughly four quarters MORE than the board assumed. Tradeability is the CRO's call — recording the fact only.

VNDA.thesis_summary: Vanda ($5.23, 60.1M sh, $315M cap) carries a hard, forward-dated FDA binary: the imsidolimab (anti-IL-36R mAb) BLA for generalized pustular psoriasis, PDUFA target action date 2026-12-12, accepted for filing 2026-02-25. The pivotal record is clean and public — GEMINI-1 met its primary endpoint (53.3% vs 13.3% GPPPGA 0/1 at wk4, p=0.0131), published in NEJM Evidence 2026-04-28, with orphan designation in the US, EU (2026-07-16) and Japan (2026-05-27). The event is idiosyncratic (a single agency decision on its own dossier) and unfired. It sits on top of a real commercial base — 2026 revenue guided $240-290M, Fanapt +26% in Q1 — that the market currently values at roughly 0.47x sales after netting cash, so very little imsidolimab value is embedded in the tape. The offsetting fact is a balance sheet running down fast: cash+ST investments fell $61.5M in Q1-26 alone, to $202.3M, and management has guided 2026 burn above 2025's.
VNDA.kill_risk: Financing gap ahead of the event. Net cash/share has collapsed from the ~$6.75 the board itself cited in 2024 when rejecting Cycle Pharma's $8.00 cash bid, to $3.37 at 2026-03-31 — Q1-26 alone consumed $61.5M of cash+ST investments, and management guided 2026 burn above 2025. A registration statement went effective 2026-05-05 (EFFECT, CIK 1347178), i.e. the shelf is armed. An equity raise between the 2026-08-05 Q2 print and the 2026-12-12 PDUFA would dilute the win leg before it pays, and every quarter of burn erodes the downside floor by roughly $0.58/sh of net cash. Second, independent risk: imsidolimab is Vanda's FIRST biologic BLA, so CMC and pre-approval-inspection failure — the modal CRL cause and entirely invisible from the efficacy record above — is not covered by the strong GEMINI-1 result. The historical "Vanda always loses at FDA" bear case (Hetlioz jet-lag CRL 2026-01-08, tradipitant gastroparesis) is the weaker objection and I discount it: FDA approved BYSANTI on 2026-02-20 and NEREUS in 2026, two on-time wins this year.

Q1-26 doubled the 2025 run-rate; management guided 2026 burn above 2025. I mark Q2-Q4-26 at a normalized $35M/qtr (below Q1's print, since Fanapt/NEREUS/BYSANTI revenue is ramping): net cash at the PDUFA = 189.6 - 3(35) = $84.6M = $1.41/sh. Both legs below are marked to THAT figure, not to today's cash - a floor computed off 3/31 cash would be ~$1.75/sh too generous by December.

WIN LEG (approval 2026-12-12) = $8.90. Commercial base at 1.0x forward revenue, 2027E ~$300M -> $300M; plus imsidolimab GPP at $150M; plus net cash $84.6M = $534.6M / 60.1M sh = $8.89, call it $8.90. The $150M GPP mark is benchmarked to SPEVIGO (spesolimab, Boehringer) - the only approved GPP therapy and the SAME IL-36R mechanism, running roughly $150-250M globally. Imsidolimab arrives second into an ultra-rare indication (~3-5k diagnosed US patients), so I carry US peak at $80-120M and value it near 1.5x peak less launch risk. I did not underwrite the GLP-1-emesis (Thetis) or CMT2S (VCA-894A) options - both are early and undated.

LOSE LEG (CRL) = $3.60. Commercial base at a distressed 0.5x 2026 revenue (0.5 x $265M = $132.5M) + net cash $84.6M = $217.1M / 60.1M = $3.61. Cross-check: the observed max-fear print this cycle is the $4.14 52wk low, set into the 2026-01-08 Hetlioz jet-lag CRL and the securities-investigation wave (Pomerantz, Levi & Korsinsky). My $3.60 sits BELOW that print deliberately - the January low was struck against a materially fatter cash balance, so the old floor is stale-HIGH here, the opposite of the usual XBI-at-highs caution.

R:R AND EV. Upside 8.90 - 5.23 = $3.67; downside 5.23 - 3.60 = $1.63; R:R = 2.25:1. EV = 0.75(8.90) + 0.25(3.60) = $7.58, or +45% vs spot.

TAKEOUT LENS - APPLIED AND REJECTED, does NOT lift the win leg. Vanda has demonstrated acquirer interest: Future Pak bid $7.25-7.75/sh (March and May 2024, latter plus CVRs) and Cycle Pharma bid $8.00/sh cash valuing Vanda at ~$466M. All were rejected unanimously; Vanda adopted a poison-pill shareholder rights plan. Three reasons I refuse to mark those comps into fair value: (1) the board's own rejection rationale was that $7.25-7.75 was "a mere 7-15% premium to Vanda's cash balance of approximately $6.75 per share" - that cash balance is now $3.37/sh, so the arithmetic underpinning those bids is gone, and the bids are stale by two years; (2) founder-CEO Polymeropoulos plus the pill make the board a demonstrated structural blocker, not a seller; (3) the 2026 record M&A tape (37 biotechs >=$1B YTD, $216B) is a LATE-STAGE, commercially-ready, >=$1B-asset phenomenon - a $315M cap whose lead asset is second-to-market behind an entrenched Boehringer product is not the scarce asset that regime is bidding for. Takeout is undated optionality only; per mandate it creates no milestone and I have not extended one.

ONE FLAG FOR THE CRO: FMP shows a $21 "consensus" price target, but targetHigh = targetLow = targetMedian = $21, i.e. a single analyst. It is 4x spot and ~2.4x my approval-leg number. Treat it as one datapoint, not a consensus - it is probably why the name is screening as edge_grade H, and it is not defensible from the live record.

ALVO.thesis_summary: Alvotech resubmitted US BLAs for AVT05 (Simponi/Simponi Aria biosimilar) and AVT06 (Eylea 2mg biosimilar) on 2026-06-04 after the Jan-2026 facility-driven CRLs; the company states it "expects the FDA to conduct a six-month review," clocking an approval decision to roughly 2026-12-04. The defect that caused the CRLs was site-specific (deficiencies from the July-2025 Reykjavik pre-license inspection), and on 2026-07-29 the FDA closed its May-2026 re-inspection of that same facility as Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) - i.e. no OAI, no approval-withholding classification. That is the single gating condition being cleared while the review clock runs, and it post-dates the board's 2026-06-08 valuation. Teva commercializes both assets. The equity is a thin stub over ~$1.53B debt and negative book equity (-$282M), so the December decision is genuinely binary at the equity level.
ALVO.kill_risk: The Q2 print on 2026-08-19 can spend the position before the catalyst ever resolves. Consensus Q2 revenue is $103M; with Q1 at $105.9M, H1 lands near $209M against unchanged FY guidance of $650-700M, requiring $441-491M in H2 - a 2.1-2.3x step-up off the H1 run-rate. A guidance cut re-rates the stub on leverage and cash burn, not on FDA odds, and there is precedent: the Jan-2026 CRL was accompanied by a slashed revenue guide and a 58% cut to adjusted EBITDA. The financing pattern corroborates stress rather than strength - $165M of equity issued at $3.75 (closed 06-17) followed by a $75M GoldenTree term loan just two weeks later (07-01). Separately, Celtic Lux (the founder vehicle) pledged 88,940,619 shares plus 7,007,321 depository receipts on 2026-06-26, ten days after buying 10.13M shares at $3.75; a pledged ~28% of the share count against a stock already near its 52-week low is a forced-sale vector that can break the $2.40 floor for reasons unrelated to the BLAs. Also note the December date is derived, not FDA-published (see dossier_note).

ALVO.dossier_note:
MILESTONE DERIVATION - READ THIS BEFORE SIZING. The 2026-12-04 date is INFERRED, not published. The trade is binary on a readout the company controls, not on the tape. The overhang is governance, not efficacy: on 2026-07-20 IMMX terminated the CMO hired in March 2026 ("Richard Graydon") after press reports identified him as Ronald Fischer, a Rhode Island fugitive of ~20 years arrested the prior week; the 8-K states the termination was for reasons unrelated to his activities at the company and no material business effect given his short tenure, but five plaintiffs' firms opened securities investigations within ten days and the stock is ~30% off its $12.14 52-week high.

XRN.thesis_summary: Chiron Real Estate (NYSE: XRN, ex-Global Medical REIT, 13.235M shares, $35.27) is mid-way through a self-directed recapitalization that converts a legacy net-lease medical-office book into a senior-housing operating (SHOP) platform. Announced 2026-05-06: $425M of Silverstone SHOP communities, a $100M delayed-draw convertible perpetual preferred led by Maewyn Capital, ~$200M of asset sales, a new debt facility, a 36% monthly dividend cut to $0.16, and withdrawal of 2026 guidance. Two legs have already fired: The Landing + The Riviera closed 2026-06-01 for $249M, and seven IRFs were recapitalized into an 85/15 JV with a US public pension fund at a $217M aggregate valuation on 2026-06-30. What remains forward is the third community, The Pinnacle North Bethesda, at ~$176M, company-guided to close October 2026 (broadened to Q4 2026 in the 06-01 release), plus the balance of the ~$200M disposition program. The equity is a sum-of-parts on depreciated real estate: management's own disclosure that the $249M of SHOP equals ~14% of the portfolio by gross real estate assets implies ~$1.78B of gross cost against $1.238B of depreciated assets and $668.6M of net debt, so roughly $540M (~$41/share) of accumulated depreciation sits between carrying value and cost. The market caps the legacy book at ~76% of gross cost; marking it at 85% and holding the two 2026 transacted assets at their own arms-length prices gets to ~$44/share. This is a NAV-discount repositioning story with a soft-dated deal close, not a hard binary event.
XRN.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the legacy net-lease medical book is worth materially more than its depreciated carrying value, and the live record pushes back hard. (1) The one completed disposition was structured as an 85/15 JV RECAPITALIZATION rather than an outright sale - that is what issuers do when an outright bid will not clear their mark; the $217M is a headline gross asset valuation, and because I cannot see JV-level debt from the record, my $32.6M mark on the retained 15% (0.15 x $217M) OVERSTATES the retained equity if the JV is levered, which it almost certainly is. (2) The ~$540M of accumulated depreciation on a physician-practice MOB book is partly real economic obsolescence, not purely an accounting artifact, and 2026 MOB cap rates sit above the 2016-2022 acquisition cap rates - so gross cost is a ceiling, not a proxy for market value. At 75% of gross cost the SoP prints $34.22, i.e. the entire discount vanishes and the market is simply right. (3) The 36% dividend cut is a direct issuer signal that the legacy book's cash generation did not support the prior payout. (4) The pivot swaps contractual net-lease income for operating risk with 2026 guidance withdrawn and Q2 consensus at -$0.235 EPS; the first print carrying SHOP economics lands 2026-08-05 AMC, one day out and entirely unpriced by this dossier. (5) The Maewyn convertible perpetual preferred ranks ahead of the common AND converts, so it clips the top of any NAV re-rating. (6) I could not reconstruct a cap-rate NAV independently: FMP's REIT line mapping is internally contradictory (Q1-26 EBITDA + G&A annualizes to ~$115M of NOI, while revenue less implied property opex annualizes to ~$56M - a 2x spread), and the SEC 10-Q and Q1 8-K exhibits returned HTTP 403, so the SoP rests on the company's own 14%/25% portfolio-mix statistic rather than on verified NOI.
